title: Coral Tissue and Skeleton Trizol RNA Extraction
author: Molly A Moynihan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bi9ikh4e

steps.title: Decontaminate work areas and tools
steps.instruction: Clean the UV hood and fume hood with bleach, ethanol, and RNaseZap; sterilize the UV hood for 15 minutes. Clean all pipette tips with bleach, ethanol, and RNaseZap. Keep UV‑hood and fume‑hood pipettes separate, use only RNA‑dedicated reagents, nuclease‑free plasticware, and filter tips.

steps.title: Thaw and homogenize samples
steps.instruction: Thaw coral tissue (already homogenized with the tissue tearor) and skeletal samples. If the suspension is too viscous, pipette it and re‑homogenize with the tissue tearor until easily pipettable.

steps.title: Add Trizol to samples
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, add 1 mL Trizol to each sample aliquot (≈200–500 µL tissue solution or 200–500 cm³ skeleton). If the aliquot contains more material than desired, transfer the excess to a new nuclease‑free 2 mL tube before adding Trizol. Phasemaker tubes may be used instead of 2 mL tubes.

steps.title: Vortex and incubate Trizol mixture
steps.instruction: Vortex the sample/Trizol mixture for 30 seconds, then incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature to dissociate nucleoprotein complexes.

steps.title: Add chloroform and mix
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, add 200 µL chloroform per 1 mL Trizol. Shake vigorously by hand, vortex briefly until the mixture is milky, and incubate for 3 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Add HCl to skeletal samples
steps.instruction: For skeletal samples only, add 1 µL to 5 µL of 6 M HCl (18.5 % HCl) to the sample/Trizol mixture.

steps.title: Prepare cold 75 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 75 % (v/v) ethanol (2 mL per sample) using molecular‑biology‑grade ethanol and store at –20 °C until needed.

steps.title: Centrifuge for phase separation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 12 000 × g, 4 °C for 15 minutes. The mixture will separate into a lower red phenol‑chloroform phase, an interphase, and a colorless upper aqueous phase.

steps.title: Recover aqueous RNA phase
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, carefully transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new 2 mL DNase/RNase‑free tube, avoiding any interphase or organic layer.

steps.title: Add isopropanol and high‑salt solution
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, add 250 µL isopropanol and 250 µL high‑salt solution (0.8 M NaCitrate/1.2 M NaCl) to the aqueous phase per 1 mL Trizol used in lysis.

steps.title: Add glycoblue and vortex
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL glycoblue (20 mg/µL) and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Incubate for RNA precipitation
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet RNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 12 000 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes. A blue gel‑like pellet (or clear/white if glycoblue was omitted) will form on the side or bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Without disturbing the pellet, carefully discard the supernatant.

steps.title: First 75 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL cold 75 % ethanol (per 1 mL Trizol originally used) and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Centrifuge first wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 7 500 × g, 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Discard supernatant after first wash
steps.instruction: Without disturbing the pellet, remove and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Second 75 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet again in 1 mL cold 75 % ethanol (per 1 mL Trizol) and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Centrifuge second wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 7 500 × g, 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Discard supernatant after second wash
steps.instruction: Without disturbing the pellet, remove and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Air‑dry RNA pellet
steps.instruction: Leave the tube lid open and air‑dry the pellet for 5 minutes to 10 minutes.

steps.title: Resuspend RNA in water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 50 µL nuclease‑free water by pipetting up and down. Incubate on a heat block at 55 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Assess RNA yield
steps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration; acceptable range is 50–300 ng/µL. If the yield is <50 ng/µL, proceed to the optional clean‑and‑concentrate protocol described below.

steps.title: Store RNA
steps.instruction: Aliquot the RNA and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare high‑salt buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 23.5 g NaCitrate in 24 mL of 5 M NaCl, then add water to a final volume of 100 mL. Autoclave, aliquot into working solutions, and keep at 4 °C. Each sample will require 250 µL of this buffer.

steps.title: Column‑based RNA cleanup – binding
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, add 100 µL RNA Binding Buffer to 50 µL of the Trizol‑extracted sample, vortex briefly, then add 150 µL 100 % ethanol and vortex briefly.

steps.title: Transfer to spin column
steps.instruction: Load the mixture onto a spin column placed in a collection tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge to bind RNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10 000 × g, room temperature, for 30 seconds. Discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash with RNA Prep Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL RNA Prep Buffer to the column, centrifuge at 10 000 × g, room temperature, for 30 seconds, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Wash with RNA Wash Buffer
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL RNA Wash Buffer to the column, centrifuge at 10 000 × g, room temperature, for 30 seconds, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Final spin to remove buffer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at 10 000 × g, room temperature, for 1 minute to eliminate residual wash buffer.

steps.title: Elute RNA from column
steps.instruction: Transfer the column to a new nuclease‑free tube. Add the desired volume of nuclease‑free water (e.g., 35–50 µL), incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes, then centrifuge at 10 000 × g, room temperature, for 30 seconds to collect the eluate.

steps.title: Cool centrifuge and handle hazards
steps.instruction: Cool the centrifuge to 4 °C before proceeding with any further steps. Perform all Trizol and chloroform transfers in a chemical fume hood; treat waste as hazardous and dispose of it properly.
